The Gibbs sampler is a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm used to approximate the posterior distribution of a Bayesian statistical model.  It iteratively samples each variable conditioned on the current values of all other variables, creating a sequence of samples that eventually converge to the true posterior.  The algorithm is particularly useful when calculating the exact posterior is computationally intractable, which is often the case in complex Bayesian models. A common application is in image reconstruction, allowing for a statistically robust approach that handles uncertainity better than traditional algorithms; it is also commonly used in advanced network modeling by using graph theory for inference.

The Gibbs sampler relies on the conditional distributions of each variable given all others.  These conditional distributions must be easily sampled from.  This is a key limitation of the Gibbs sampler – if the conditional distributions are not straightforward to sample from, the algorithm may be inefficient or impossible to implement.  The process continues until the Markov chain has reached a steady state, meaning the chain's transitions become stationary.
